mainTopic: The reward for מעשר, the stories of ריש לקיש's son, and whether פרנסה can come for one person
overview: The גמרא reads 'עשר תעשר' as a promise: give מעשר and you will become rich. In a story, רבי יוחנן tells ריש לקיש's young son to 'go test it.' The boy objects that testing God is forbidden, and רבי יוחנן answers in the name of רבי הושעיא that מעשר is the one exception, from a פסוק in מלאכי. In a second story, the boy shows רבי יוחנן that the idea of a פסוק in משלי (a person causes his own trouble and then blames ה׳) is hinted in the תורה, in the words of יוסף's brothers. The boy's mother then pulls him away from רבי יוחנן. Next, רבי יוחנן teaches that rain can come for one person, but פרנסה only comes for the many. A ברייתא says the מן came in the merit of משה alone, which seems to contradict this. The גמרא answers that משה asked on behalf of the whole people, so he counts like the many. The amud ends by beginning a story about רבא's students who came to learn from רב פפא, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Tithe so that you will become wealthy
steps.stepSummary: A דרשה on the doubled words 'עשר תעשר': give מעשר so that you will become rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A tithe shall you tithe' means: give a tithe so that you will become wealthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the doubled verb 'עשר תעשר' as a hint: give מעשר, and you will become rich.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second word 'תעשר' sounds like 'תתעשר' (you will become rich), since ש and שׂ look alike. So the פסוק is read as both a command and a promise of reward.

keyTerms.meaning: A tithe, one tenth of produce
So that you will become wealthy

steps.whyThisMatters: This promise is the base for everything that follows: the story, the question about testing God, and the exception for מעשר.

phrases.english: "A tithe shall you tithe"
Tithe so that you will become wealthy.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן meets the son of ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: רבי יוחנן asks ריש לקיש's young son which פסוק he learned, and the boy says 'עשר תעשר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן found the young son of ריש לקיש. He said to him: Tell me your verse! The boy said: 'A tithe shall you tithe.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that sets up a conversation about the דרשה we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking a child 'what פסוק did you learn today?' was a common practice. The boy's answer happens to be the exact פסוק from step 1, which leads into the discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: Tell me your verse (the one you learned)

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְיָנוֹקָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan found the young son of Reish Lakish,
He said to him: Tell me your verse!
He said to him: "A tithe shall you tithe."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְיָנוֹקָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story built around the פסוק from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: the boy names the פסוק 'עשר תעשר'.

steps.title: The boy asks what the verse means
steps.stepSummary: The boy asks רבי יוחנן what the doubled words 'עשר תעשר' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And what does 'A tithe shall you tithe' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The boy asks for the meaning of the doubled wording. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the repeated verb. A doubled word in the תורה invites a דרשה, so the boy wants to know what extra meaning is hidden there.

phrases.english: He said to him: And what is "A tithe shall you tithe"?
phrases.notes: Following Sefaria: the boy asks רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the פסוק the boy just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the doubled phrase 'עשר תעשר'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן explains the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers with the same דרשה: tithe so that you will become wealthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Give a tithe so that you will become wealthy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the boy the דרשה from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the דרשה is said directly by רבי יוחנן in the story. It is a promise of reward, which leads the boy to ask for proof.

phrases.english: He said to him: Tithe so that you will become wealthy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled verb means: give מעשר and you will become rich.

steps.title: The boy asks for a source
steps.stepSummary: The boy asks רבי יוחנן how he knows this promise is true.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: From where do you know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The boy asks for proof that giving מעשר really brings wealth. This sets up רבי יוחנן's surprising answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wordplay is a hint, not a proof. The boy wants a firmer basis for such a big promise.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?

phrases.english: He said to him: From where do you know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of the answer in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source or proof that giving מעשר brings wealth.

steps.title: Go and test it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers: go and test it yourself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go and test it.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of quoting a source, רבי יוחנן tells the boy to try it and see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof offered is experience: give מעשר and watch the reward come. This answer opens the door to the boy's challenge about testing God.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go and test it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The proof is to test it and see the result.

steps.title: But testing God is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The boy challenges: the תורה says 'לא תנסו את ה'', so how can one test God?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And is it permitted to test the Holy One, Blessed be He? But it is written: 'You shall not test ה׳!'
steps.whatsHappening: The boy attacks רבי יוחנן's answer by quoting a פסוק that forbids testing God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said 'go test it,' but the תורה (דברים 6:16) says not to test ה׳. So his advice seems to tell the boy to do something forbidden.

phrases.english: He said to him: And is it permitted to test
the Holy One, Blessed be He?
But it is written: "You shall not test the Lord"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי שְׁרֵי לְנַסּוֹיֵיהּ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'go test it' answer of step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'לא תנסו את ה'' forbids testing God, so one cannot be told to test Him.

steps.title: Tithes are the one exception
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רבי הושעיא, רבי יוחנן answers that מעשר is the exception, because in מלאכי ה׳ Himself says 'test Me' about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: So said רבי הושעיא: Except for this, as it says: 'Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in My house, and test Me now with this, says ה׳ of hosts, if I will not open for you the windows of heaven and pour out for you blessing until there is no more need.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge: the ban on testing God has one exception, מעשר, and he proves it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'לא תנסו' still stands in general. But in מלאכי 3:10 ה׳ openly invites people to test Him with מעשר, so in this one case testing is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Testing God is generally forbidden, but מעשר is the one exception, because ה׳ Himself says 'test Me' about it in מלאכי.
steps.confusionAlert: The rule 'לא תנסו את ה'' is not cancelled. מעשר is only an exception to it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: He said to him: So said Rabbi Hoshaya:
Except for this, as it is stated:

phrases.aramaic: ״הָבִיאוּ אֶת כׇּל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר אֶל בֵּית הָאוֹצָר
phrases.english: "Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse,
that there may be food in My house,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְחָנוּנִי נָא בָּזֹאת אָמַר ה׳ צְבָאוֹת
phrases.english: and test Me now with this, says the Lord of hosts,

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא אֶפְתַּח לָכֶם אֵת אֲרֻבּוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם
phrases.english: if I will not open for you the windows of heaven

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרִיקֹתִי לָכֶם בְּרָכָה עַד בְּלִי דָי״.
phrases.english: and pour out for you a blessing until there is more than enough."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא: חוּץ מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception to a general rule, based on a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Testing God is forbidden with no exceptions, so 'go test it' is wrong advice.
steps.terutzMaskana: Testing God is forbidden, except with מעשר, where ה׳ says 'ובחנוני נא בזאת'.

steps.title: What does 'until there is no more need' mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses the story to ask the meaning of 'עד בלי די' in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'until there is no more need'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps aside to explain an unclear phrase from the פסוק in מלאכי. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'עד בלי די' literally mean 'until without enough,' which is unclear. The גמרא wants to know how big the promised blessing is.

phrases.english: What is "until there is more than enough"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side question about a phrase in the פסוק quoted in step 8.

steps.title: Until your lips wear out from saying 'enough'
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא quoting רב explains: the blessing will be so great that your lips will wear out from saying 'enough'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said in the name of רב: Until your lips wear out from saying 'enough.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains 'עד בלי די' as a picture of overflowing blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'בלי' like 'יבלו' (wear out) and 'די' as 'enough.' You will say 'enough!' so many times that your lips get worn out.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said that Rav said:
Until your lips wear out from saying "enough."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing will be so great that your lips wear out from saying 'enough'.

steps.title: The boy's closing remark
steps.stepSummary: Back in the story, the boy says that had he reached that פסוק himself, he would not have needed רבי יוחנן or רבי הושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If I had reached that verse there, I would not have needed you or הושעיא your teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the story, and the boy ends it with a bold remark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The boy means the exception for מעשר is written openly in the פסוק, so he could have figured it out alone. It shows the boy's sharpness, much like his father ריש לקיש.
steps.whatToRemember: The permission to test ה׳ with מעשר is written openly in מלאכי 3:10.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הֲוָת מָטֵי הָתָם לְהַאי פְּסוּקָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: If I had reached that verse there,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוֵית צְרִיכְנָא לָךְ וּלְהוֹשַׁעְיָא רַבָּךְ.
phrases.english: I would not have needed you or Hoshaya your teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הֲוָת מָטֵי הָתָם לְהַאי פְּסוּקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story after the side explanation in steps 9 and 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The exception allowing one to test ה׳ with מעשר comes straight from the פסוק in מלאכי.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן finds ריש לקיש's son reciting a verse
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. רבי יוחנן finds the young son of ריש לקיש reciting a פסוק from משלי about a person who sins and then blames ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time, רבי יוחנן found the young son of ריש לקיש sitting and saying the פסוק: 'A man's own foolishness ruins his path, and then his heart is angry at ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second story about the same clever boy. This line sets up the scene and the פסוק that the next steps will discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a person who causes his own trouble through sin, and then complains to ה׳ as if ה׳ were to blame. This פסוק will become the subject of רבי יוחנן's question in the next step.

phrases.english: And furthermore, Rabbi Yochanan found
the young son of Reish Lakish
who was sitting and saying:
"The foolishness of a man ruins his way,
and his heart is angry at ה׳."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְיָנוֹקֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a second story about the same boy from the previous story (steps 2–11).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scene is set: the boy is reciting משלי יט:ג, about a person who sins and then blames ה׳.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן wonders where this idea is hinted in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן is puzzled. He assumes everything in כתובים has a hint in the תורה, but he cannot find the source for this פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן sat and wondered. He said: Is there anything written in כתובים that is not hinted at in the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן asks a real question: where in the תורה is the idea of this פסוק from משלי found?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption behind the question is that every idea in כתובים has its root in the five books of the תורה. רבי יוחנן cannot find the root for this idea, so he is surprised. The question sets up the boy's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The Writings, the third part of תנ"ך (including משלי)
The תורה (the five books of משה)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying that the idea is missing from the תורה. He believes it must be there and is puzzled because he cannot find it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan sat and was wondering.
He said: Is there anything
that is written in the Writings
that is not hinted at in the Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דִּכְתִיבִי בִּכְתוּבֵי דְּלָא רְמִיזִי בְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks where the פסוק quoted in step 12 is rooted in the תורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where in the תורה is the idea of משלי יט:ג hinted at?

steps.title: The boy shows the hint from יוסף's brothers
steps.stepSummary: The boy answers that the idea is in the תורה. When the brothers of יוסף found their money returned, they said 'What is this that God has done to us?', even though their own sin had caused their trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: The boy said to him: Do you really think it is not hinted at? It is written: 'Their hearts sank, and they turned trembling to one another, saying: What is this that God has done to us?'
steps.whatsHappening: The boy answers רבי יוחנן's question by quoting a פסוק from בראשית that shows the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers of יוסף were in trouble because they had sold יוסף. Yet they asked, 'What has God done to us?', as if it came from nowhere. That is exactly the message of משלי: a person causes his own trouble and then turns to ה׳ in complaint.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (rejects an assumption)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: אַטּוּ הָא מִי לָא רְמִיזִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: Is that to say this is not hinted at?
But is it not written: "Their hearts sank, and they trembled
phrases.notes: בראשית מב:כח, the brothers of יוסף

phrases.english: each man to his brother, saying:
What is this that God has done to us?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ הָא מִי לָא רְמִיזִי, וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's question from step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The idea is hinted at in בראשית מב:כח. The brothers caused their own trouble and then asked what God had done to them.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן stares and the mother pulls the boy away
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן stares at the boy in amazement. The boy's mother takes him away, afraid that רבי יוחנן will do to him what happened to his father, ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן raised his eyes and looked at him. The boy's mother came and took him out. She said to him: Come away from him, so that he does not do to you what he did to your father.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The mother removes her son from רבי יוחנן's presence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's look shows amazement at the boy's sharp answer. The mother remembers that ריש לקיש died after a painful dispute with רבי יוחנן. She fears that the gaze of such a great צדיק could harm her son as well.
steps.confusionAlert: 'What he did to your father' refers to the famous story (בבא מציעא פד.) in which ריש לקיש died after a dispute with רבי יוחנן. It does not mean that רבי יוחנן deliberately harmed anyone.
steps.whatToRemember: The boy proved that the idea of משלי (blaming ה׳ for trouble you caused yourself) is already found in the תורה, in the words of the brothers of יוסף.

phrases.english: He raised his eyes and looked at him.
His mother came and took him out.
She said to him: Come away from before him,
so that he does not do to you as he did to your father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story after the boy's answer in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story ends with רבי יוחנן's amazement and the mother protecting her son.

steps.title: Rain can come for one person, sustenance only for many
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי יוחנן's series of teachings about rain. Rain can fall for the sake of one person, but a blessing of פרנסה comes only for the sake of a community.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Rain can come for the sake of one person. פרנסה comes only for the sake of many.
steps.whatsHappening: After the stories, the גמרא brings a new teaching of רבי יוחנן. The next step will prove both halves from פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two kinds of blessing are compared. Rain can be sent because one deserving person prays or merits it. A general blessing of food and livelihood needs the merit of a whole community.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of one individual

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מָטָר בִּשְׁבִיל יָחִיד,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: Rain comes for the sake of an individual;
sustenance comes for the sake of many.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מָטָר בִּשְׁבִיל יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the series of רבי יוחנן's statements about rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain can be given in the merit of one individual. Sustenance is given only in the merit of a community.

steps.title: Proof from singular 'you' versus plural 'you'
steps.stepSummary: Each half of רבי יוחנן's rule is proven from a פסוק. The rain פסוק uses 'לך' (singular you). The bread-from-heaven פסוק uses 'לכם' (plural you).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rain for one person, as it says: 'ה׳ will open for you (singular) His good storehouse, to give rain to your land.' Sustenance for many, as it says: 'I will rain down bread for you (plural).'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a פסוק to support each part of his rule from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is from grammar. 'לְךָ' is singular, so rain can come even for one person. 'לָכֶם' is plural, so the bread from heaven (the מן) came for the whole nation. That shows that sustenance comes for the many.
steps.confusionAlert: Both פסוקים use 'rain' language. The second פסוק is about bread (the מן) raining down, and that is why it teaches about פרנסה.
steps.whatToRemember: Rain can come in one person's merit (לְךָ, singular). Sustenance comes in the merit of the community (לָכֶם, plural).

phrases.english: Rain for the sake of an individual, as it is written:
"ה׳ will open for you (singular) His good storehouse
to give the rain of your land."
Sustenance for the sake of many, as it is written:
"Behold, I will rain down bread for you (plural)."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for each half of the rule stated in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule: rain for an individual, sustenance for many.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the מן came in the merit of משה alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. It lists three leaders and three gifts. The מן is credited to משה, a single person. This seems to contradict רבי יוחנן's rule that פרנסה comes only for a community.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises a challenge from a ברייתא. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: three good leaders rose up for the Jewish people: משה, אהרן, and מרים. Three good gifts were given through them: the well, the cloud, and the מן. The well was in the merit of מרים. The pillar of cloud was in the merit of אהרן. The מן was in the merit of משה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 16. It quotes a ברייתא saying the מן (bread, which is פרנסה) came in the merit of one man, משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said rain can come for one person, but פרנסה only comes for a community. The ברייתא gives each gift to one person, and the מן goes to משה alone. If one person's merit brought the מן, then פרנסה can come for an individual, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They challenged': the גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack a statement
Leaders who provide for and take care of the people
The miraculous well that gave water in the מדבר
The pillar of cloud that guided and protected the people
The bread from heaven that fed the people in the מדבר

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not about rain or about רבי יוחנן directly. The challenge comes only from one detail: the מן, which is פרנסה, came in the merit of one person. The ברייתא continues through step 24. The גמרא then spells out the challenge in step 25 and answers it in step 26.

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: They challenged: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
Three good leaders rose up for Israel,
and they are: Moshe, Aharon, and Miriam.

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁלֹשׁ מַתָּנוֹת טוֹבוֹת נִיתְּנוּ עַל יָדָם,
phrases.english: And three good gifts were given through them,
and they are: the well, the cloud, and the manna.
The well: in the merit of Miriam,
the pillar of cloud: in the merit of Aharon,
the manna: in the merit of Moshe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule that was stated in Step 16 and proven in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a blessing of פרנסה comes only for the sake of a community.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מן is פרנסה, and the ברייתא says it came in the merit of one individual, משה.

steps.title: When מרים died, the well disappeared
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves from פסוקים that the well depended on מרים. Right after the פסוק of her death, the next פסוק says there was no water. The well later came back in the merit of משה and אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: When מרים died, the well disappeared. As it says: 'And מרים died there,' and right after it is written: 'And there was no water for the congregation.' The well came back in the merit of both of them (משה and אהרן).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It shows from the order of the פסוקים that the well left when מרים died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from two פסוקים that sit right next to each other: מרים dies, and right away there is no water. This shows the well was tied to her merit. The well then returned because of the merit of the two remaining leaders.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is written right after it

phrases.english: When Miriam died, the well disappeared,
as it says: 'And Miriam died there,'
and it is written right after it: 'And there was no water for the congregation,'
and it returned in the merit of both of them.
phrases.notes: Both of them means משה and אהרן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and backs up its claim that the well was in מרים's merit.
steps.raayaObject: The well depended on מרים's merit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר כ:א-ב: the death of מרים is followed right away by 'there was no water.'

steps.title: When אהרן died, the clouds of glory disappeared
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves that the ענני כבוד left when אהרן died. The king of ערד 'heard' something and attacked. What he heard was that אהרן had died and the clouds had left. A second פסוק is brought to support this.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אהרן died, the clouds of glory disappeared. As it says: 'And the Canaanite, the king of ערד, heard.' What news did he hear? He heard that אהרן died and the clouds of glory had left. He thought he now had permission to fight against Israel. This is what is written: 'And all the congregation saw that אהרן had died.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves that the clouds depended on אהרן. It explains why the king of ערד suddenly attacked: he saw the clouds were gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say what the king heard, so the ברייתא fills it in: אהרן died and the protecting clouds left. That is why the king felt free to attack. The second פסוק, 'all the congregation saw,' is brought as more support, and the next step explains how it fits.

keyTerms.meaning: The clouds of glory that surrounded and protected Israel
And this is what is written

phrases.english: When Aharon died, the clouds of glory disappeared,
as it says: 'And the Canaanite, the king of Arad, heard,'
What news did he hear?
He heard that Aharon had died
and the clouds of glory had disappeared,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְסָבוּר נִיתְּנָה לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְהִלָּחֵם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: and he thought he had been given permission to fight against Israel.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּרְאוּ כׇּל הָעֵדָה כִּי גָוַע אַהֲרֹן״.
phrases.english: And this is what is written: 'And all the congregation saw that Aharon had died.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת אַהֲרֹן נִסְתַּלְּקוּ עַנְנֵי כָּבוֹד, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the same pattern as Step 19, now for אהרן and the clouds.
steps.raayaObject: The ענני כבוד depended on אהרן's merit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The king of ערד's attack after אהרן's death, plus the פסוק 'ויראו כל העדה כי גוע אהרן.'

steps.title: רבי אבהו rereads the פסוק as 'they were seen'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains how the פסוק 'all the congregation saw' hints at the clouds leaving. Read it as 'they were seen': without the clouds, the people were exposed. ריש לקיש's teaching that כי can mean 'because' makes the reading work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Do not read it as 'and they saw.' Read it as 'and they were seen.' This follows ריש לקיש's teaching, for ריש לקיש said: the word כי is used in four meanings: 'if,' 'perhaps,' 'but,' and 'because.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו explains how the פסוק from Step 20 really shows that the clouds left. He gives it a new reading, and he uses ריש לקיש's rule about the word כי to support it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק says the people 'saw that' אהרן died, which says nothing about clouds. רבי אבהו reads 'they were seen,' meaning the people were now visible because the clouds no longer covered them. ריש לקיש's rule that כי can mean 'because' (דהא) lets the פסוק read: 'the congregation was seen, because אהרן had died.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not read': a style of דרשה that rereads a word with different vowels
A word with several meanings, here 'because'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two words. וַיִּרְאוּ means 'they saw.' In this דרשה, the new reading means 'they were seen,' that is, the people became exposed once the clouds were gone.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אַל תִּקְרֵי ״וַיִּרְאוּ״, אֶלָּא ״וַיִּירָאוּ״.
phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said: Do not read 'and they saw,' but rather 'and they were seen.'

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְדָרֵישׁ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: As Reish Lakish taught, for Reish Lakish said:
The word 'ki' is used in four meanings:
'if,' 'perhaps,' 'but,' and 'because.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted at the end of Step 20 fits the claim that the clouds left.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Read the פסוק as 'the congregation was seen, because (כי = דהא) אהרן died.' The people were exposed once the clouds left.

steps.title: When משה died, all three gifts ended
steps.stepSummary: The well and the clouds came back in משה's merit. When משה died, all three gifts left. The ברייתא brings a פסוק in זכריה about cutting off three shepherds in one month.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both came back in the merit of משה. When משה died, all of them disappeared. As it says: 'And I cut off the three shepherds in one month.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its story: after משה died, nothing was left. It brings a פסוק, and the next step questions that פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now משה's merit was holding up all three gifts, so his death ended all of them together. The פסוק about 'three shepherds' is meant to show this. Read literally, though, it raises a problem, which the next step points out.

keyTerms.meaning: The three shepherds: משה, אהרן, and מרים

phrases.english: Both of them returned in the merit of Moshe,
when Moshe died, all of them disappeared,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וָאַכְחִד אֶת שְׁלֹשֶׁת הָרֹעִים בְּיֶרַח אֶחָד״,
phrases.english: as it says: 'And I cut off the three shepherds in one month.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the pattern of Steps 19 and 20 with the death of משה.
steps.raayaObject: All three gifts ended with משה's death.
steps.raayaSupportSource: זכריה יא:ח: 'And I cut off the three shepherds in one month.'

steps.title: They did not all die in one month
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges the literal reading of the פסוק. The three leaders died in three different months: מרים in ניסן, אהרן in אב, and משה in אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did they really die in one month? Didn't מרים die in ניסן, אהרן in אב, and משה in אדר?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא attacks the simple meaning of the פסוק it just quoted. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the three shepherds were cut off 'in one month.' But the known dates of their deaths are spread over three different months. So 'in one month' cannot mean that they all died in one month.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And is it so?': a challenging question
The months when מרים, אהרן, and משה died

phrases.english: But did they die in one month?
Didn't Miriam die in Nisan,
and Aharon in Av, and Moshe in Adar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal meaning of the פסוק quoted in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal meaning of 'three shepherds in one month.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their deaths are dated to three different months, so they could not all have died in one month.

steps.title: The gifts, not the leaders, ended in one month
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the פסוק means the three gifts given through the three leaders all ended in one month, when משה died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches that the three good gifts that were given through them were cancelled, and all of them disappeared in one month.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question from Step 23. The 'one month' is about when the gifts ended, not when the leaders died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each leader's gift was kept going after their death by the leaders still alive. Only when משה died did all three gifts stop together, in one month. So it is as if all three shepherds were 'cut off' at the same time.

keyTerms.meaning: Were cancelled, came to an end

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא: well = מרים, cloud = אהרן, מן = משה. Each gift left when its leader died and came back through the others, until משה's death ended all three. The point that matters for the sugya is that the מן came in one man's merit, משה. That is the challenge to רבי יוחנן. The גמרא states it in step 25 and answers it in step 26.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the ברייתא. The challenge from Step 18 now stands in full: פרנסה (the מן) came in the merit of one person. The next two steps spell out this challenge and answer it.

phrases.english: Rather, it teaches that there were cancelled

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ מַתָּנוֹת טוֹבוֹת שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ עַל יָדָן,
phrases.english: the three good gifts that were given through them,
and all of them disappeared in one month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means the three leaders died in one month.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק means the three gifts all ended in one month, at משה's death.

steps.title: So פרנסה Can Come for One Person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the challenge from the ברייתא: the מן came in משה's merit, so פרנסה can come for one individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows that we find sustenance coming for the sake of a single individual!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the problem that the ברייתא creates. The ברייתא said the מן came because of משה, so it looks like פרנסה can come for just one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule said rain can come for one person, but פרנסה only comes for the many. The ברייתא said the מן, which is פרנסה, came in the merit of משה alone. That seems to contradict the rule directly.

keyTerms.meaning: It follows that / apparently (we see from this that)
For the sake of a single individual

phrases.english: Apparently, we find sustenance
phrases.notes: The מן is the sustenance being discussed.

phrases.english: for the sake of an individual!
phrases.notes: In the merit of משה alone. This contradicts the rule that פרנסה comes only for the many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenging conclusion out of the ברייתא that was just explained, and turns it against the earlier rule about פרנסה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that פרנסה comes only בשביל רבים (for the many).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the מן, a form of פרנסה, came in the merit of משה, a single person. So פרנסה can come for an individual.

steps.title: משה Counts Like the Many
steps.stepSummary: משה is different because he asked on behalf of the whole people, so he is treated like the many.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה is different. Since he asked for the many, he is considered like the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. משה is a special case because he asked for food for all of Israel, not for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule stays in place: פרנסה comes only for the many. משה's request was for the whole community, so his merit counts as the merit of the many. The case of the מן is therefore not a real exception.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule stands: פרנסה comes only for the many. A leader who asks on behalf of the whole community counts like the many.

phrases.english: Moses is different,
since he requested it for the many,
phrases.notes: He asked for food for all of Israel.

phrases.english: he is considered like the many.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי מֹשֶׁה, כֵּיוָן דִּלְרַבִּים הוּא בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: משה is a special case, not a true individual.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the מן came in משה's merit, it looked like פרנסה can come for one person.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה asked on behalf of the community, so he counts as רבים. The rule about פרנסה remains intact.

steps.title: רבא's Students Move to רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: three students of רבא came to learn from רב פפא after רבא died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר מנוח, רב שמואל בר אידי, and רב חייא from ווסתניא were often found before רבא. When רבא died, they came before רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story connected to the פסוק in זכריה about 'three shepherds.' This line sets the scene: three of רבא's top students began learning with רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three were great scholars who were used to learning from רבא. When they move to a new teacher, רב פפא, the story's tension is set up. The connection to the 'three shepherds' פסוק will appear as the story continues.

keyTerms.meaning: Were regularly found before him (his regular students)

steps.confusionAlert: This story is not a new halachic argument. It is an אגדה, a story, that the גמרא brings because it connects to the פסוק in זכריה quoted earlier.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Manoaḥ
and Rav Shmuel bar Idi
and Rav Ḥiyya from Vastanya
were often found before Rava.
phrases.notes: They were his regular, distinguished students.

phrases.english: When Rava died,
they came before Rav Pappa,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר מָנוֹחַ וְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִידִי וְרַב חִיָּיא מִוּוֹסְתַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about פרנסה and opens a story tied to the פסוק of the 'three shepherds' from step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: three of רבא's students began learning under רב פפא after רבא's death.

steps.title: The Students Signal to Each Other and רב פפא Is Hurt
steps.stepSummary: When רב פפא's teachings did not make sense to them, the students gestured to one another, and רב פפא was offended.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whenever he told them a teaching and it did not seem reasonable to them, they would signal to each other. He was offended.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The students showed their disagreement through quiet gestures, and רב פפא felt hurt. This sets up what happens next in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students did not openly challenge רב פפא. Instead they hinted to each other, as if saying he was not on רבא's level. The phrase חלש דעתיה, 'he was offended,' signals that a consequence is coming in the next part of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: They hinted / gestured to one another
He was offended (literally: his mind was weakened)

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֵימַת דַּהֲוָה אָמַר לְהוּ שְׁמַעְתָּא
phrases.english: whenever he would tell them a teaching
and it did not seem reasonable to them,
they would gesture to one another.
phrases.notes: They hinted that רב פפא was not equal to רבא.

phrases.english: He [Rav Pappa] was offended.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל אֵימַת דַּהֲוָה אָמַר לְהוּ שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in step 27 and sets up its next development.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: the students' silent signals of disagreement hurt רב פפא's feelings.
